To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated a panel of chimeric DEN1 viruses that contain the C, M, and E genes or ME genes of the DEN4 vaccine strain, rDEN4.

we generated four chimeric DEN1 viruses using the CME or ME structural genes and a 30nt deletion in the 3′ untranslated region (Δ30) and found that rDEN1Δ30(ME, Δ30) induced 66 percent seroconversion and conferred protection from DEN1 virus challenge in rhesus macaques.
rDEN1Δ30(ME)/4 is a safe and immunogenic candidate vaccine against DEN1 and that the Δ30 mutation is associated with attenuation in mice and rhesus monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of vaccines against dengue virus, the most prevalent arbovirus infection worldwide.
the development of a dengue vaccine that is effective against the four serotypes of the dengue virus.
the generation of a dengue virus vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work provides the first report on the development of a DEN1 chimeric vaccine and the first demonstration of the utility of the Δ30 attenuating mutation in DEN4 chimeric viruses.
the DEN1 chimeric virus, rDEN1-4Δ30ME, is a promising candidate for further development as a vaccine against dengue.
rDEN1/ME-4Δ30 is the best candidate for further evaluation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DEN4 backbone is an ideal platform for development of a live attenuated dengue vaccine candidate, but that the Δ30 mutation is necessary for attenuation in primates.
the chimeric virus with the C gene and Δ30 mutation is over-attenuation, while the chimeric viruses that contain the Δ30 mutation and either the M or E gene of DEN1 were attenuated and protective.
rDEN1-4Δ30(MEME) is a good candidate for a vaccine against dengue virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Δ30 deletion is a useful tool for attenuating chimeric DEN viruses and that the C gene of the DEN4 vaccine backbone can be replaced with that of a DEN1 strain.
the Δ30 mutation is critical to the attenuation of chimeric DEN viruses in non-human primates.
the DEN4 backbone is a suitable platform for the development of chimeric vaccines for other serotypes of DEN.
